column1: # with sdk- are rewritten by tools/symbols/match_libs.py. Add your own with the source user. The
# type is a C type from game/types.h or the SDK's headers, and the comment goes above the global.

column5: The id of Kamui's last texture DMA request, which kmyCopyToTexture writes. kmQueryFinishLastTextureDMA and so njLoadTextureFinishDMA check whether it has finished.
The game's copies of the two controllers, made each frame by gameReadPad.
Shinobi's records of the two controllers.
The scene that runs: 1 boot, 2 logos, 3 rankings (sceneRankingStart), 4 title, 5 mode select, 6 to 10 the chapters, 11 tutorial, 12 ending.
The scene to change to at the next frame, 0 for none.
The scene that follows the stage, which each chapter's start and the tutorial's start set. stageCmdEnd and the tutorial's exit in stageDraw change to it.
The 7 task lists, each its first and last task.
Set to 1 when the disc tray opens, when gameFrame returns nonzero, or at a controller reset in the attract mode or in scene 1. gameMain's loop then ends, but not while a save is being written.
MONITOR TYPE: 1 for the two horizontal types, 0 for the two vertical ones. optionsApply copies it to screenHorizontal, and saveCalcSum sums the save block from this byte on.
1: gameReadPad turns the pads' directions a quarter turn (left to down, right to up, up to left, down to right). The config menu sets it only with a vertical monitor type.
AUTO SAVE: 1, gameEnterScene writes the save to the card when saveRequest is set. The backup menu toggles it, and a failed save sets it to 0.
1: the horizontal screen at 75%, 0: at 80%.

Four bits that open the appendix menu's items: 0x2 the first gallery, 0x1 the second gallery, 0x4 the sound test and 0x8 the game mode choice. The ending sets 0x1 for a clear, 0x4 or 0x8 for a clear without continues at easy or normal, 0x2 for a trial clear without continues, and playTimeAdd sets 0x2, 0x1, 0x4 and 0x8 after 5, 10, 15 and 20 hours of play.
1: the prototype mode, in which shots cost energy.
Set: the next scene change saves to the card, with optionAutosave on.
Each player's spare lives, without the ship in play. playerStart sets gameLives - 1, scoreAdd adds one at extendScore, and a ship lost at 0 puts the player out.

The stage's scroll, the position along the stage's path that pathAt reads. stageUpdate adds scrollSpeed each frame and stops it at the path's end, and stage commands and scripts wait until it reaches their positions.
The scroll's speed, a float, which moves toward scrollTarget.
Each player's score.
The fade's four corners, a polygon over the whole screen.
Each player's ship (Player).

Each player's directions and buttons in this frame, held and newly pressed: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, 0x10 shot, 0x20 switch, 0x40 release. playerReadInput makes it from the controller, demoInputRead from the recorded input.
Each player's energy for homing lasers: a release fires one laser for each 10, up to 12. It holds up to 120, or up to 999 in the prototype mode, where shots spend it too.
Each player's polarity, 0 or 1, which playerSetPolarity keeps and playerCreate gives the ship at the next stage start. playerStart sets it to 0.
Each player's shot button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonShot.
Each player's switch button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonSwitch.
Each player's release button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonRelease.
Each player's setting that shot and switch pressed together release too.
The controller bits of the 7 button choices of the controller settings: A, B, R or C, X, Y, L or Z, and none.
The number of members in each of the 4 script groups.
The 4 stage script groups, up to 256 members each, which a record can wait to be empty.
Each player's current set of kills: its color in the high 4 bits and its kills in the low 4.
Each player's chain: the completed sets of three kills of one color in a row.
Each player's longest chain in this stage. stageStart clears it, and chapterScoresStore keeps it for the chapter.
Each player's score for the next extra life.
The game's EXTEND, which optionsApply copies from optionExtend. playerStart and scoreAdd read it.
The 200 objects that homing lasers can aim at, with where each was drawn and the damage on its way to it.
This frame's hit records, in 5 lists: ships, fields, shots, enemies and bullets.
The laser slot of the object hit this frame, whose hit points the gauge shows.
The players in the game, a bit each: 0x01 player 1, 0x02 player 2. playerStart sets a player's bit, and a hit with no spare life clears it.
1 in the prototype mode.
The pause: 1 paused, 2 to pause at the next frame.

The players who hold the pause, a bit each. pauseUpdate sets it to 1 or 2 for the player who pressed Start, and the pause menu clears a player's bit. At 0 the pause menu ends the pause, and gameTaskFrame counts gameFrames only while it is 0.
A 1 here ends the pause.
1 while the pause holds the sound.

The players who cannot pause, a bit each. gameEnterScene locks both, a chapter's start unlocks the players in the game, joining or continuing unlocks a player, and losing the last ship or going out locks the player again.

1 in the attract mode: set after the boot's card check, at the end of a game and when the main menu is left, and cleared by Start on the title. The demos, the logos and the title before Start run with it.
What happened in this frame, cleared by stageUpdate: 0x02 the bullets vanish.
The speed that the scroll moves toward.
How much the scroll's speed moves toward its target in a frame.
The read position in the recorded input of a demo or the tutorial, which demoStart sets and stageStart clears. While it is not 0, demoInputRead gives player 1's ship this input instead of the pad's.

The stage's lock bytes: command 2 raises the first, command 3 waits until stageUnlock lowers it to 0, command 4 waits for any byte from here to be 0, and the ease commands hold one as their task's lock. stageStart clears 20 bytes from here, which also hold playersContinuing, nameEntryPlayers, gameOver and stageEvents.
A counter that stage command 3 raises. Command 6 and stageStart set it to 0.
A counter that the stage program raises (command 6).
The stage program's commands by number. See docs/game.md, The stage program.
1 in the practice mode, which returns to the title after the chapter.
The stage path's point at scrollPosition, from pathAt. The camera orbits about it, and the draws of objects on the path start from it.
The stage path's three angles at scrollPosition, from pathAt. stageUpdate adds them to the camera's orbit, and the draws on the path turn by them.
The path's seventh value at scrollPosition.
The camera's structure (Camera), while a camera task lives.
The game's slot for each of the 8 sequence players (soundSequencePlayers): the sequence to play, its level and pan, and its state. soundServer starts, pauses and resumes the players from it.
The game's slot for each of the 20 one-shot players (soundEffectPlayers): the sound to play, its level and pan, and its state. soundServer starts, pauses and resumes the players from it.
The sound library's 8 MIDI sequence players.
The sound library's 20 one-shot players.
The 4 loaded lists of sound banks. Slot 0 holds SFX_DEFAULT.BIN's.
The file names of the sound bank lists.
1: no sound starts.
1: sounds get a pan and a volume from their position.
The game's difficulty: 0 easy, 1 normal, 2 hard.
The random numbers' state.
The data of the hit point gauge's task, which hpGaugeCreate makes at the stage start. hpGaugeSet puts the hit points of the object in gaugeSlot into it.
The save block's identifier, IK-BKUP 1.2.
The sum of the save block's other bytes (saveCalcSum).
TRIAL GAME: 1, GAME START goes to the mode select, which offers the trial game (gameTrial). The config menu toggles it, and it is 1 by default.
DIFFICULTY: 0 EASY, 1 NORMAL, 2 HARD, or 3 USER SELECT, which chooses at the mode select (difficultyChoice). optionsApply sets difficulty from it.
PLAYER STOCK: the lives at the start, 1 to 5 and 3 by default. optionsApply copies it to gameLives.
EXTEND: 0 none, 1 one every 2,000,000, 2 one at 3,000,000 and then every 5,000,000 more, 3 one at 6,000,000 and one at 15,000,000. optionsApply copies it to gameExtend.
Each player's shot button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, A by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonShot.
Each player's switch button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, B by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonSwitch.
Each player's release button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, R or C by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonRelease.
Each player's setting in CONFIG that shot and switch pressed together release too, 1 by default. playerJoin copies it to buttonShotSwitch.
The HUD's offset in x, in steps of 4 from -28 to 12, which left and right change in the pause menu. hudPlace and the other HUD draws move the HUD by it, the other way for player 2.
The HUD's offset in y, in steps of 4 from -28 to 12, which up and down change in the pause menu. hudPlace and the other HUD draws move the HUD by it.
Each player's vibration, on or off.
The credits that sceneTitleStart gives a game, 3 at first. playTimeAdd adds one for each hour of play up to 9, and an hour after that sets 0xFF, free play.
For each difficulty, the highest chapter that a game reached without a continue, 1 at first. PRACTICE offers the chapters up to it.
The play time at which the next credit comes.
The seconds of play, up to 1,000 hours.

The rankings: 4 tables of 12 lists of 20 entries (RankEntry), which rankingDefaults fills. rankingFindPlaces and rankingAdd use the table of difficulty, lists 0 to 5 for one player and 6 to 11 for two.
The card file's header.
The card file's image while the card reads or writes it.
The game's PLAYER STOCK, which optionsApply copies from optionLives and demoStart takes from the demo's record. playerStart gives one less as spare lives.
The difficulty chosen at the mode select, in the practice menu or for the tutorial, 1 at power-on. While optionDifficulty is 3, optionsApply sets difficulty from it.
The credits left in this game. 0xFF: free play.
The frames since the game's start, without those while a player holds the pause (pausePlayer). playTimeAdd turns them into seconds of playTime.
The game's copy of optionHorizontal, which optionsApply makes. With 0, a vertical screen, screenPlace turns 2D positions a quarter turn and cameraFlat turns the view.
The game's copy of optionScreen75.
Each player's continues, up to 255. A player who joins starts with it as the score, up to 9.
This game's place in each of the 6 ranking lists, 0xFF for none.
1 once both players are in the game.

Three blocks of 6 entries, each a score and a longest chain, for player 1, player 2 and both players together (chapterScoresTotal), with the game's total in entry 0 and each chapter's part in entries 1 to 5. rankingFindPlaces compares them with ranking lists 0 to 5, or for two players with lists 6 to 11.
The disc's directories that fileSetDir changes to.
The file that the disc reads now.
Where the disc read goes.
The size of the file that the disc reads.
The 16 graphics banks (Bank): models, sprites and a texture list each.

Room for 128 scenery polygons (SceneryPolygon), an origin and a polygon each. sceneryAdd adds them during a frame, sceneryClear empties them each frame, and sceneryHit tests the ships, shots, lasers and bullets against them.
The number of polygons in sceneryPolygons.
The state of the VMU screen in the first socket of each controller (ports A1 and B1): 0 none, 1 to 8 what to show, 9 writing it. vmuScreenEvent picks what to show, and vmuScreenUpdate runs it.
1 in a trial game.
1 in a game that enters no ranking: a practice or a trial.
The players at the name entry.
The frames since gameInit.
The players at the continue, a bit each.
Each player's 1 once a join counts as a continue.
The continue's countdown, from 9.
1 once the game over runs.
The cursor of the title menu that runs. In the controller settings it is player 1's cursor, and the next byte player 2's.
The title's screen. See docs/game.md, The title and its menus.
The count of attract demos, which titlePressStart raises before each one. Its value mod 3 picks the demo: 0 the tutorial, 1 chapter 1, 2 chapter 2.
The seconds left on the boss timers whose bosses died in time, which bossTimeAdd sums and stageStart clears. The results pay 10,000 points for each second (BOSS DESTROY BONUS).
The seconds left on the boss's timer.

A count of requests for each of the 4 vibration units (sockets 1 and 2 of each controller), which vibrationStart raises. A vibration task whose count is no longer the current one ends without starting.
